items.title: Alexander's subbase theorem: a finite-refinement test on a subbase implies quasi-compactness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file topology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is Alexander's subbase theorem in the form the chapter uses (author lemma at source lines 2182-2187, label lemma-subbase-theorem, bearing the author's own bracketed name): a subbase whose coverings always have finite refinements forces the space to be quasi-compact. The proof (source lines 2189-2210) is the classical Zorn argument, complete in the author's own presentation: it chooses a maximal covering without a finite refinement (proof lines 2190-2196), shows that the members lying in the subbase already cover the space (proof lines 2196-2204), applies the hypothesis to obtain a finite refinement, and uses maximality a second time to turn that refinement into a finite subcovering of the original covering, giving the contradiction (proof lines 2204-2210). The theorem is the tool by which the chapter verifies quasi-compactness of spectral spaces and of limits. H2.
